title: Kinematics

points.text: Displacement, velocity and acceleration as derivatives
Displacement versus total distance from integrals of velocity

bigPicture: Kinematics is calculus applied to motion along a line: differentiate to go from displacement to velocity to acceleration, integrate to go back.

keyIdeas.cue: How are displacement, velocity and acceleration linked?
keyIdeas.answer: v = ds/dt; a = dv/dt = d²s/dt². At rest: v = 0. Speed = |v|. Speeding up when v and a have the same sign.
Change in displacement from t₁ to t₂ = ∫ v dt (signed). Total distance = ∫|v| dt; on the GDC integrate |v| directly, by hand split at the times where v = 0.

keyTerms.def: signed position relative to the start or origin

workedExamples.title: Distance by hand
workedExamples.prompt: v(t) = t² − 4t + 3, 0 ≤ t ≤ 3. Find the displacement and the total distance.
steps: v = 0 at t = 1: ∫₀¹ v dt = 4/3, ∫₁³ v dt = −4/3

practice.prompt: s(t) = t³ − 6t² + 9t. Find when the particle is at rest and its acceleration at those times.
v(t) = 2 sin t − 0.5t m/s for 0 ≤ t ≤ 6. Find the displacement and the total distance travelled.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
